title: Getting Started
text:
In these workshops, we will use the Bioinformatics Core training server. This server provides access to a Linux environment, course data and pre-installed bioinformatics tools. Contact Shaun Webb for an account.
If you are using the Bioinformatics Core servers, please abide by our user policy and best practices: https://drp-hcb-bioinformatics.github.io/DRP-HCB-Bioinformatics/user_policy.html
If you would like to use your own Linux environment, a list of software versions will be provided at the start of each course. See below for installing software with Conda.

title: Getting Started
text:
Terminal applications
To access the server, you will need to use the Terminal application on your local machine. Windows, Mac and Linux computers all have a built in Terminal application. There are also many third party Terminal applications if you desire a more stylish or interactive setup.

title: Getting Started
text:
Accessing the server
The ssh command is used to connect to a remote server and stands for “secure shell”.
ssh -Y username@bifx-core1.bio.ed.ac.uk
The -Y option allows you to run graphical applications on the server and have them displayed on your local machine. Replace username with your university UUN (universal user name).

title: Getting Started
text:
Installing software
Not required if using the Bioinformatics Core servers.
We recommend Conda for installing software on your own Linux environment. Conda is a package manager that allows you to install software and manage dependencies in isolated environments.
Follow our guide to setting up a Conda environment here: https://drp-hcb-bioinformatics.github.io/DRP-HCB-Bioinformatics/software.html#managing-your-own-software-tools-and-packages-with-conda

title: Getting Started
text:
Project management
It is good practice to keep your work organised in a project folder. This will make it easier to revisit your work in the future. Best practice is to create a new project for each course and keep all of your work in that project folder.
If you are using Conda to install software, it is also good practice to create a new Conda environment for each project. This will help avoid conflicts between software versions and dependencies.

title: Analysing Sequencing Data
text:
This is the homepage for Analysing Sequencing Data hosted by the DRP-HCB Bioinformatics Core at the University of Edinburgh.
These courses are run annually by the Bioinformatics Core but are also available upon request.

title: Analysing Sequencing Data
text:
Course content

Lesson 1: Bioinformatics on the Linux command line
Lesson 2: High throughput sequencing data
Lesson 3: Analysing HTS data (ChIP-seq example)
Lesson 4: Long read transcriptomics
Lesson 5: Building bioinformatics pipelines (bash scripts and Snakemake)


For more information contact Shaun Webb.
